lots.title: Provision of Planned and Preventative Corporate Building Maintenance (PPM) & Remedial Repairs excluding full replacements
lots.description: Lot 8 of the London Borough of Bexley Framework 6278 (Building Services Framework - Lots 1-11). This draft T&Cs document is the contractual wrapper governing the Contractor's provision of building services (planned and preventative maintenance of corporate buildings together with remedial works excluding full replacements) to The Mayor and Burgesses of the London Borough of Bexley. The T&Cs themselves do not enumerate the inspection cadence, asset list, response times, KPI values, trade / craft breakdown or Service Credit tables for Lot 8 - those live in Schedule 1 (Specification) and Schedule 4 to the Specification (KPIs / Service Credits), which appear only as placeholder headings at the end of this draft. What the document does fix is: the quality regime (BSI / ISO Quality Standards and Good Industry Practice), the 'Annual Fee Services' construct tied to the PPM Schedule in Appendix B to the Specification, the construction-contract special conditions (CDM Regulations 2015, principal designer / principal contractor duties, BSI codes of practice, COSHH register, CIMAR-based adjudication / arbitration), the staffing regime (DBS, fluent English contract manager, key personnel), insurance minima via Schedule F, the data-protection split (Council = Controller, Contractor = Processor), and standard statutory obligations (Bribery Act 2010, Public Contracts Regulations 2015, UK GDPR / DPA 2018, Equality Act 2010, Electronic Invoicing Regulations 2019, Local Government Act 1999 - Best Value). The template Contract Period on the front matter is 1 September 2020 to 31 August 2024 and must be treated as boilerplate; the authoritative dates and value for Lot 8 come from the live Framework 6278 notice. The notice-level metadata records an anticipated Lot 8 value of ~£860k per annum and places the lot in PSQ Group 2.

lots.title: Provision of Reactive Repairs to Corporate Building

As with Lot 8, the substantive scope (types of defects in scope such as the notice-level examples of gutter clearance and boarding-up, response-time SLAs, dispatch / Works Order protocol, pricing mechanism, key asset list and KPI / Service Credit regime) is defined by reference to Schedule 1 (Specification) and Schedule 4 to the Specification, which appear only as placeholder headings in this draft. The template Contract Period on the front matter (1 Sep 2020 - 31 Aug 2024) is boilerplate; the authoritative dates and value for Lot 9 come from the live Framework 6278 notice. Notice-level metadata records an anticipated Lot 9 value of ~£175k per annum and places the lot in PSQ Group 2.

evidence_anchors.anchor_text: AGREEMENT ... RELATING TO THE PROVISION OF BUILDING SERVICES ... THE MAYOR AND BURGESSES OF THE LONDON BOROUGH OF BEXLEY ... [THE CONTRACTOR]
evidence_anchors.section_ref: Part 1 Form of Contract title block

evidence_anchors.anchor_text: The Council wishes to secure the provision of building services as defined in the attached Specification ('the Services') during the period 1 September 2020 to 31 August 2024

(d) The Specification appended hereto as Schedule 1; (e) The Pricing Schedule appended hereto as Schedule 2; (f) The Council's ITT appended hereto as Schedule 3; (g) The Contractor's Proposal ... appended hereto as Schedule 4
'Annual Fee Services' means the services described in the Appendix B to the Specification (PPM Schedule)
'CDM Regulations' means the Construction (Design and Management) Regulations 2015

'Quality Standards' means the quality standards published by BSI British Standards Institution, the National Standards Body of the United Kingdom, the International Organisation for Standardisation or other reputable or equivalent body
The Contractor shall supply the Services during the Contract Period in accordance with the Council's requirements as set out in the Specification
Timely supply of the Services shall be of the essence of the Contract
The Contractor shall provide all the Equipment necessary for the supply of the Services.
The Contractor shall at all times comply with the Quality Standards, and where applicable shall maintain accreditation with the relevant Quality Standards authorisation body.
The Contractor shall at his expense register with the Disclosure and Barring Service and where required by the Specification undertake appropriate criminal records checks

an electronic invoice complies with the standard on electronic invoicing where it complies with the standard referred to in the Public Procurement (Electronic Invoices etc.) Regulations 2019 (2019/624)

any chemicals or other solutions or substances or materials used for the purposes of the Services will comply with any particular requirements set out in the Specification ... and in every case shall conform with any relevant British or European standard and in the case of chemicals have full approval from the Health and Safety Executive or Environment Agency
the Council is the Controller and that the Contractor is the Processor unless otherwise specified in Schedule 1

The Contractor shall perform all the functions and duties of a "principal designer" and a "principal contractor" as defined in the CDM Regulations (including the preparation of the "Construction Phase Plan" and the "Health and Safety File" in accordance with the CDM Regulations) to the extent that the CDM Regulations are applicable to the Services
The Contractor shall service the Plant and maintain it in good working order and in accordance with the provisions of any manufacturer's guarantees or recommendations
contravene any relevant standard code of practice issued from time to time by the BSI Group or under a European directive relating to standards or good building practice

do not accord with the guidelines contained in the edition of the publication "Good Practice in Selection of Construction Materials" (British Council for Offices ("BCO")), current at the date of specification or use
maintain a COSHH register for all substances stored at or brought onto the Premises by the Contractor or any Staff, which shall be up-to-date at all times
the Contractor shall ensure that its health and safety policy statement (as required by the Health and Safety at Work etc Act 1974) is made available to the Council on request

the following acts or omissions are a non-exhaustive list of unacceptable practices at the Premises: S4.1.1 a failure properly to dispose of refuse within the same Working Day; S4.1.2 the throwing of bags, sacks or other heavy items from balconies, walkway, bridges
The Arbitration shall be conducted in accordance with the CIMAR Rules
